messages:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's key rotation we started seeing AccessDenied on Decrypt for a cross-account Lambda that assumes role: logs show "User: arn:aws:sts::222222222222:assumed-role/ci-lambda-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt". Anyone seen this pattern after rotation?

sam: Can you paste the key policy and the role's trust/inline policies? Often it's either policy scope or missing grant token in callers.

maria: Key policy (redacted): 
```json
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[{
    "Sid":"AllowAccountUse",
    "Effect":"Allow",
    "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::111111111111:root"},
    "Action":["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt"],
    "Resource":"*"
  }]
}
```
Role inline policy (snippet): 
```json
{"Action":["kms:Decrypt"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef12","Effect":"Allow"}
```
Trust policy: standard sts:AssumeRole for lambda.

jonah: Two possibilities: 1) The principal on the key policy is the root of 111..., but the caller is an assumed role in account 222... so you need to allow the assumed-role principal (or the role ARN) explicitly in the key policy, or 2) if using a grant earlier, grant tokens are required while rotating. Which account actually owns the key? Looks like key in 111111111111 and lambda runs in 222222222222.

maria: Key is in account 111111111111. We used envelope encryption via KMS on producer side in account 111. The consumer lambda in 222 calls Decrypt with ciphertext from producer. That used to work pre-rotation.

kevin: Did you check if there are grants on the key that allowed the 222 account via a service principal? Run: 
```
aws kms list-grants --key-id alias/my-prod-key --profile prod
```
If a grant existed and you rotated or re-created the key material, grants may have been removed. Also check CloudTrail for kms:CreateGrant/DeleteGrant around rotation time.

maria: Ran list-grants — returned empty. CloudTrail shows a DeleteGrant event at rotation. Oops.

sam: That explains it. Grants can be used to permit specific AWS services/principals to use CMKs without putting the principal explicitly in the key policy. If you relied on a grant that got deleted during rotation, add either: 1) a key policy statement allowing arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/ci-lambda-role to kms:Decrypt, or 2) recreate the grant for that role.

jonah: Note: if the decrypt is happening via the AWS Encryption SDK or a KMS-generated data key, the caller sometimes needs to pass the grant token returned at CreateGrant time. If your consumer code never stored the grant token and the grant got created and deleted during rotation, Decrypt will fail. To test locally: 
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://blob.bin --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef12 --profile consumer --debug
```
Look for MissingGrantToken or AccessDenied messages.

maria: The consumer does not use any grant token currently. We had assumed key policy + role policy were enough. Why did it work before?

kevin: Possibility: pre-rotation there was a long-lived grant that allowed the Lambda's role or service principal (e.g., lambda.amazonaws.com) to use the key. During rotation process (we used an automation) the grant was removed and not re-issued. Or the key was re-created (not just rotated) so ARNs changed. Check key-id vs alias mapping: 
```
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/my-prod-key
```
Confirm keyId didn't change.

maria: describe-key shows key-id is same but the rotation automation re-applied a policy that only included account root. That removed the explicit role statement we had previously added manually.

sam: Two remediation paths: 
- Short term: create grant scoped to the role and include the GrantToken in the consumer if you control it. Commands: 
```
aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/ci-lambda-role --operations Decrypt --name "ci-consumer-grant"
```
This returns a GrantToken you can optionally pass to callers.
- Permanent: update key policy to include the cross-account role principal and add condition on aws:PrincipalArn if you want narrow scope.

jonah: Also watch for encryption context: if the producer used EncryptionContext when generating the ciphertext, the consumer's Decrypt must provide the same context or KMS will deny. CloudTrail will show kms:Decrypt with error If encryption-context mismatch.

maria: Producer used EncryptionContext {"app":"publisher-service"}. Consumer does NOT pass context. But it worked before — could the grant circumvent the context requirement?

kevin: Grants don't bypass encryption-context checks. So if it worked before, either the original producer didn't use context OR the consumer was passing it. CloudTrail for Decrypt will show the provided encryption context. Check event details.

maria: Found older logs: consumer used to pass the context, but a refactor removed that param. So two failures coincided: key policy rollback + missing context. No wonder it broke after rotation.

sam: Good find. Action items: 
- maria: re-add required encryption-context in consumer, create a short-lived grant to restore service ASAP, and update key policy automation to include role principal.
- kevin: audit rotation automation to avoid policy resets that remove principals/grants.
- jonah: add an integration test that decrypts a sample blob across accounts after rotation.

maria: Doing the grant now and patching consumer to send context. I'll post updates. :thumbsup:

kms-bot: Detected new grant create: grantId = 3a1b-xxxx. Created by maria at 1719453600.

maria: Grant applied and consumer now decrypts successfully when sending the correct encryption-context. Confirmed in staging. Closing for now, will follow up with a PR to rotation automation.

kevin: Nice triage — saved us from prolonged incident. Recommend we document this cross-account envelope rotation checklist in runbook.
